children: Investment group Bollore is set to stop production of electric buses at manufacturer Bluebus and streamline its battery maker, potentially affecting more than 100 jobs in the face of hotter competition and other challenges in Europe's automotive and battery industries.

Discontinuing production at Bluebus will affect some 74 employees, with a smaller organization remaining in place to provide support for buses already in operation, Bollore said in a release Tuesday. A European industrial company active in transportation is looking at acquiring Bluebus's research & development activities, a move that could save 17 of the jobs envisaged to be cut, the company said, without naming the suitor.

A sister company that makes lithium batteries for electric vehicles, Blue Solutions, is meanwhile set to streamline its organization in order to "advance its technology toward industrial scale alongside a strategic investor," Bollore said. The restructuring aims to respond to a "fundamental shift in the competitive landscape and meet the increasingly demanding expectations of its partners," Bollore said. Some 41 positions are in line to be affected at Blue Solutions.

Since its founding, Bluebus has deployed close to 700 electric buses to urban and suburban services in France and across Europe, Bollore said, noting the manufacturer's "meaningful contribution to the development of low-carbon mobility."

But slower-than-expected growth in its home market, combined with intense competition and pricing pressure, means Bluebus has struggled to reach the scale needed to compete with other industry players, said Bollore, whose holdings also include stakes in the likes of Universal Music Group and broadcaster Canal+.

"Following years of exploring strategic alternatives and taking significant steps to adapt its business model, the company has determined that the conditions necessary for sustainable long-term manufacturing operations no longer exist," the group said.
